parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the need to clone Python idna/test3.py in pure ESM, preserve exact argparse, repr, IDNA/UTS46, punycode, stdout, and produce /output/test3.mjs.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It split work across four children: punycode implementation, IDNA/UTS46 table extraction, executable behavior probing, and pyrepr/argparse implementation; the parent planned later core integration, entry assembly, and fuzzing.
parallel.implementation: Two component children completed verified punycode and argparse/pyrepr modules. The table child wrote extractor/test scripts but left the long extraction running. The behavior child gathered probes and disassembly but never returned a report.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No final integration happened. The copied artifact contained helper modules, probes, and cache files, but not /output/test3.mjs and not a completed idnaTables.mjs.
parallel.verification: Component tests passed for punycode and argparse/pyrepr. There was no integrated whole-program test against the evaluator-facing entry point because that entry point was never assembled.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Core IDNA logic, completed generated tables, behavior.md, integrated test3.mjs, and end-to-end differential tests were all missing or incomplete at closure.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same exact pure ESM migration, black-box executable probing, argparse bool semantics, IDNA edge behavior, and final entry-file requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor kept all work local, using a todo list that still had probing, table extraction, module writing, test3.mjs writing, and differential testing pending.
serial.implementation: The serial actor performed many executable probes and source/binary inspections but did not write reusable implementation modules or the entry file before cancellation.
serial.integration_and_delivery: There was no integration stage and the artifact directory was empty, so the required /output/test3.mjs was absent.
serial.verification: Verification consisted of local exploratory probes against the executable; no generated JavaScript implementation existed to run through unit or end-to-end tests.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial attempt stopped during analysis with all implementation, table extraction, entrypoint, and differential testing work pending.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized exact ESM migration, no external dependencies, black-box behavior matching, local module split, and final test3.mjs delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had the same prompt and recognized the same IDNA, argparse, output, and final entry-file requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was similar; the difference was that parallel split requirements into child scopes while serial kept them in one todo-driven flow.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel delegated four workstreams and left final core integration, entry assembly, and fuzzing for later parent phases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no children and placed probing, extraction, module writing, entry file, and differential tests in one local todo list.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained concurrent component progress but depended on child handoffs before integration; serial avoided delegation overhead but never left the investigation phase.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel gave self-contained child briefs for distinct components, but the table child owned a huge generated-interface dependency and the behavior child never returned its spec.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial maintained all discovered behavior and pending work in one context without cross-agent handoff interfaces.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had coordination boundaries for data tables and behavioral findings; serial had no handoff boundary but also no deliverable progress.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced verified punycode and argparse/pyrepr modules and scripts for table extraction, but not the IDNA core or final entry point.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial executed probes and binary/source inspections but did not write any implementation files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel created partial reusable implementation artifacts; serial produced only investigative evidence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Three children returned to the parent, but one returned with table extraction still running and the behavior child was stopped before completion.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; the main actor was canceled directly while still probing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel accumulated incomplete child lifecycle states that blocked assembly, while serial's unfinished state was a single local cancellation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote multiple partial files into /output and leaked shared TodoList state across child contexts, but never assembled a coherent final tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no shared child workspace and copied an empty artifact tree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had partial shared-state artifacts and a tool-state contamination episode; serial had no inter-agent shared state but also no files.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had passing component checks for punycode and argparse/pyrepr, but no integrated evaluator-aligned test of test3.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran exploratory probes only and never had a JavaScript artifact to verify.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verified components but not the whole product; serial verified behavior observations but no implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out after a long multi-agent attempt; one child had relaunched a three-hour extraction and another child was canceled before returning.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, with its todo list still showing extraction, module writing, entrypoint, and differential testing pending.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted the run budget, but parallel spent it across incomplete child workstreams while serial spent it in one deep investigation stream.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluations failed 0/19. Parallel and serial differed materially in process and artifact shape: the parallel run created partial component modules and helper scripts but missed the final entry point and completed IDNA tables, while the serial run remained in local probing and produced an empty artifact. The retained labels describe parallel-side adverse coordination episodes, not a cause of a discordant score.
parallel_contributors: Created verified punycode and argparse/pyrepr components but did not integrate them into /output/test3.mjs.
Assigned full Unicode IDNA/UTS46 table extraction to one child that returned while the extraction was still running.
Lost the behavior-probe child before its requested behavior.md summary returned.
serial_contributors: Stayed in a single exploratory stream and never wrote implementation files.
The todo list still had table extraction, module writing, entrypoint, and differential testing pending when the run canceled.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The underlying IDNA migration is broad and table-heavy; both runs failed to reach full implementation, independent of the parallel coordination labels.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No outcome difference: both failed; retained patterns are parallel adverse process consequences, not exclusive root causes of a discordant result.

candidates.reason: Parallel had implementation owners for punycode, table extraction, behavior probing, and argparse/pyrepr; the failure was incomplete execution and final assembly, not absence of any implementation owner.
The parent explicitly planned later core integration and fuzzing after child results, so integration was deferred rather than unowned.
The missing test3.mjs is real, but the parent plan reserved final entry assembly for a later phase; explicit parent ownership defeats this Missing Owner label.
The end-to-end pipeline was not ownerless; it was blocked by unfinished child work and cancellation before the planned integration/test phase.
Productive component implementation ran concurrently with investigation; the work was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight.
The parent did not complete all investigation as a first phase before implementation; punycode and argparse/pyrepr implementation occurred during the same parallel phase.
The critical table path was not merely starved while auxiliary work consumed capacity; it was specifically assigned as an overbroad single-child sweep, which is the more precise retained label.
Four children were launched, but the concrete unfinished critical path is traceable to one oversized table-extraction child rather than excessive breadth or repeated fan-out.
One child received the dominant all-code-point IDNA/UTS46 table reconstruction and was still running a checkpointed extraction when it returned, leaving an indispensable module absent.
candidates.realized_consequence: The required generated IDNA table module was not delivered, so final assembly could not produce the required test3.mjs entrypoint.
candidates.near_match_reason: The adverse chain centers on one oversized child assignment, not collective exhaustion from too many simultaneous children.

candidates.reason: The retained failures are not caused by an already-known requirement omitted from a child brief; the table and behavior children were given the relevant deliverables and failed to finish.
The child scopes were separated by file/module boundaries; there is no observed incompatible independently produced interface that required unplanned reconciliation.
No known finding is shown being omitted or lost through a transfer and then causing repeated work or an incorrect action by the receiver.
Completed child reports were not too voluminous to consume; the more direct problems are an incomplete table result and a canceled behavior child.
No child result describing a superseded workspace or decision state was consumed by the parent to make an inconsistent next step.
The parent did not receive incompatible child reports or contracts that remained unadjudicated at an integration decision point.
The parent never presented the whole task as complete or accepted a final implementation; the run timed out with missing artifacts.
The table child did restart extraction, but it explicitly added checkpointing and crash-aware parsing, so the retry was not checkpoint-free or unchanged.

Completed component results were visible, but the missing final program is better explained by unfinished critical dependencies and cancellation before planned assembly, not a distinct unjoined completed implementation.
The stopped behavior child was a probe/spec child, not a completed verifier with a trapped concrete finding; Early Child Termination captures the lifecycle boundary.
The behavior child failure arrived at closure after explicit cancellation, leaving no distinct evidenced parent takeover decision separate from the retained termination event.
The parent did receive completed component summaries, but it was canceled before a decision point that proceeded inconsistently with an ignored result.
The parent did not simply wait blindly; child progress and results were returned, and the direct issues are an oversized table child plus active behavior-child cancellation.
Children wrote distinct component files and helper scripts; no competing implementation paths with overlapping behavior were observed to require reconciliation.
No evidence shows two live agents editing the same source/configuration file and one observing or reconciling the other's concurrent edit.
No agent replaced or deleted non-entry source produced by another agent; edits remained within owned component files.
No required entry point existed to be overwritten, and no child replaced another agent's submitted deliverable.
There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion that replaced multiple current outputs or invalidated another agent's final-tree work.

Agents did write under the same /output tree, but there is no proven unstable implementation state or provenance problem from shared source writes; the retained shared-state issue is tool-state leakage.
A TodoList state created by one child was injected into unrelated child contexts as current task state, and the argparse/pyrepr child then cleared it while other workstreams were active.

candidates.near_match_reason: The shared object was the orchestration TodoList state, not a source file or implementation workspace write collision.
